title: Test-Time Training with Diversified Local Aggregation Consistency for Mortality Prediction using Clinical Time Series

problem.claim: Mortality prediction for ICU patients must remain accurate when clinical time-series data come from different domains.

gap.claim: Existing models struggle with domain shifts, privacy constraints hinder cross-domain calibration, and test-time training for clinical time series must address temporal imbalance that can bias predictions toward dense local patterns.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes DLAC-TTT, a test-time training method for clinical time series.
DLAC-TTT enforces local diversity and global consistency across distinct temporal distributions within each patient through aggregation during test-time updates.
The method aims to reduce reliance on specific local patterns and integrate diverse local patterns for global learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe DLAC-TTT as a novel test-time training method with diversified local aggregation consistency.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show improved generalization performance across real-world clinical datasets from different medical institutes.

narrative_sequence.summary: ICU mortality prediction relies on clinical time series for accurate predictions.
Cross-domain shifts and privacy constraints make model deployment and calibration difficult.
Test-time training adapts a source model to each target sample, but clinical time series introduce temporal imbalance that can bias the model toward dense local patterns.
DLAC-TTT uses local diversity and global consistency through aggregation across patient-specific temporal distributions.
The authors report improved cross-institute generalization on real-world clinical datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the clinical datasets, cohort sizes, baselines, metrics, or effect sizes.
The abstract does not describe the training objective, aggregation procedure, or adaptation protocol in implementation detail.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported experimental results.
